title: B2B Telemarketing Services Cost: Rates, Minimums and Retainers
desc: B2B telemarketing costs under $25 an hour at 36 of 42 Clutch providers, about $67 to $150 per appointment on our packages, or from $2,497 to build an AI caller.
keywords: b2b telemarketing services cost, telemarketing services pricing, outsourced telemarketing cost per hour, appointment setting services cost, cost per qualified appointment b2b, telemarketing company rates, b2b cold calling services price, outsourced sdr cost, ai calling system cost, telemarketing compliance costs
cta: Want to compare our appointment packages with your current telemarketing spend?
body:
Short answer. B2B telemarketing services are sold three ways, and each has a published price point you can check. By the hour, most outsourced call centres advertise under $25 an hour: on Clutch's telemarketing rankings page read on 2 November 2026, 36 of the 42 providers on the first page list a rate under $25 an hour, 4 list $25 to $49, 1 lists $50 to $99 and 1 lists $150 to $199, with 31 of the 48 minimum-project badges we counted reading $1,000 and up, 10 reading $5,000, 3 reading $10,000, 2 reading $50,000 and 2 reading $100,000. By monthly package sized in appointments, our own lead generation plans are $2,997 a month for 20 to 40 qualified appointments, $5,997 for 40 to 80 and $9,997 and up for 80 to 150 or more, which works out at roughly $67 to $150 per appointment. And by the system, an AI calling deployment is $2,497 one-time to build and from $1,997 a month to run. The number that none of those prices includes is compliance: $500 per violation under the TCPA, state registrations from $50 to $1,500 with bonds up to $100,000, and the seller's possible vicarious liability for a vendor's calls. Here is each model with its figures and the questions to ask before signing.

Model one: hourly rates on the marketplaces

Clutch's Top Telemarketing Companies page for November 2026 shows a self-reported hourly band and minimum project size on each provider card. On the first page of 42 providers the distribution was: under $25 an hour, 36 providers; $25 to $49, 4; $50 to $99, 1; $150 to $199, 1. The minimum project badges we counted read $1,000 and up on 31 of the 48 badges, $5,000 and up on 10, $10,000 and up on 3, $50,000 and up on 2 and $100,000 and up on 2; some badges sit outside provider cards, so treat the split as indicative. Sample cards at under $25 an hour with a $1,000 minimum included Unity Communications (Gilbert, Arizona), Prialto (Portland, Oregon), Remote CoWorker (Hollywood, Florida), Hit Rate Solutions (Chicago), Leadium (Las Vegas) and Wing Assistant (Berkeley); Helpware CX (Lexington, Kentucky) listed a $5,000 minimum, 1840 & Company (Overland Park, Kansas) $10,000 and FlairsTech $50,000. ContactPoint 360 and Paragon Sales Solutions (Countesthorpe, England) sat in the $25 to $49 band.

Two things to know about these numbers. The bands are entered by the providers themselves on their Clutch profiles, and the list order is Clutch's ranking. And an hourly rate under $25 buys an agent's time, not a result: dial lists, scripts, data, telephony and the compliance layer are either billed separately or your problem. In the under-$25 band a 160-hour month for one full-time agent is under $4,000 (for example $3,840 at an assumed $24 an hour) before any of that.

Model two: monthly packages sized by qualified appointments

The second model prices the output. Our lead generation page lists Growth at $2,997 a month for 20 to 40 qualified appointments, Scale at $5,997 a month for 40 to 80, and Enterprise at $9,997 and up a month for 80 to 150 or more; Growth includes a dedicated SDR. The implied cost per appointment is the package price divided by the appointments delivered:

PackageMonthly priceAppointmentsCost per appointment
Growth$2,99720 to 40$74.93 to $149.85
Scale$5,99740 to 80$74.96 to $149.93
Enterprise$9,997 and up80 to 150 or more$66.65 to $124.96 at $9,997

Our pricing page shows two related lines: outbound campaigns that book qualified demos at $2,497 a month on the Growth plan and from $4,997 a month on Scale, and a cold email plus LinkedIn pipeline programme at $1,997 a month on Growth and from $3,997 on Scale. The difference between an hourly agent and an appointment-sized package is what the fee is tied to: hours dialled, or a stated range of booked meetings, so the definition of "qualified" is the clause to read first.

Model three: build the calling system

The third model replaces or augments agents with software. Our AI calling pages for insurance and mortgage lending price it the same way: "Build $2,497 one-time, from," a compliant AI calling system live on your stack in 2 to 4 weeks, and "Managed $1,997 /month, from," where we run it, tune it and keep it compliant. Telephony, the voice engine, list screening and CRM usage are billed by those vendors directly. Year one, if both are bought, is $2,497 plus twelve months at $1,997, or from $26,461, plus any third-party usage. The use cases that fit are inbound qualification and consented follow-up at volume; cold outbound by an AI voice runs into the consent and state rules below, which is why our pages describe the build as a compliance layer plus a dialer rather than a dialer alone.

The price nobody puts on the card

Whichever model you buy, the seller can carry legal exposure for calls made on its behalf. Four cost lines belong in the comparison:

  1. Federal damages. The TCPA gives a called party $500 per violation, which a court may raise up to threefold for willful or knowing violations, and the FTC's Telemarketing Sales Rule sits alongside it. A hundred unlawful calls is $50,000 at the base figure and up to $150,000 at the top. Under the FCC's 2013 DISH ruling a seller "may be held vicariously liable under federal common law principles of agency" for a vendor's calls, as we set out in TCPA vicarious liability.
  2. State registration. Six of the seven states in our registration-by-state hub require a telemarketer registration or licence, at $50 (California) to $1,500 (Florida), with security of $10,000 (Texas), $25,000 (New York), $50,000 (Pennsylvania) and $100,000 (California). California's registration reaches only sellers whose pitch meets Business and Professions Code 17511.1 (prizes, below-regular-price claims, investments, loans and similar pitches); the other five write their own business-to-business exemptions: New York exempts calls between a telemarketer and any for-profit business except retail sales of nondurable office or cleaning supplies; Florida and Pennsylvania exempt B2B sellers with three years under one name and at least 50 percent of dollar volume from repeat sales to existing businesses; Texas exempts sales to businesses that resell or manufacture with the goods and calls to existing customers by a seller with two years under one name; Washington's Department of Revenue excepts sales to businesses that resell the product or use it for manufacturing. Selling a service to a company for its own use fits neither Texas's nor Washington's resale exception; New York exempts most calls to for-profit businesses, and Pennsylvania's Act covers only consumer goods or services.
  3. Calling windows and robocall rules. The federal window in 47 CFR 64.1200(c)(1) applies to telephone solicitations to residential subscribers, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. at the called party's location, and the FTC's Telemarketing Sales Rule exempts most calls to businesses under 16 CFR 310.6(b)(7), except calls to sell nondurable office or cleaning supplies; Florida and Washington stop at 8 p.m.; Pennsylvania stops at 7 p.m. and bans Sunday solicitations since 18 October 2026; Texas and Georgia require permits for recorded-message dialers and Washington bans unsolicited commercial robocalls. A vendor's dialer has to hold those rules per number.
  4. Abandonment and opt-outs. Predictive dialers that drop calls and opt-out requests that are not honoured are two ways an outsourced campaign can generate claims; the rules are in the TCPA abandonment rate rule and TCPA opt-out requirements.

Comparing the three models on one campaign

Take a campaign that needs 30 qualified appointments a month into a US B2B list. On the hourly model, one full-time agent in the under-$25 band is under $4,000 a month (for example $3,840 at an assumed $24 an hour) before data, telephony and compliance, and the appointment count depends on the list and the agent. On the appointment model, Growth at $2,997 is priced for 20 to 40 appointments, so 30 lands at $99.90 each. On the system model, the AI build is from $2,497 once and from $1,997 a month, and it earns its keep on inbound and consented volume rather than on cold dials. The honest comparison is not price per hour against price per appointment; it is total monthly spend against booked, qualified meetings, with the compliance exposure assigned to whoever is making the calls.

Seven questions before you sign

  1. What exactly counts as a qualified appointment, and what happens to the fee when one no-shows or disqualifies?
  2. Who supplies and scrubs the list, against the national registry and which state lists, and how often?
  3. Which states are registered, under which exemption do the rest rely, and can you see the certificates?
  4. What hours does the dialer enforce, by the called party's local time, and where are the state cutoffs set?
  5. What is the abandonment rate, how is it measured, and what does the dialer do when a call is dropped?
  6. How are opt-outs captured and shared back, and in what time?
  7. What is the minimum project size and the notice period, and does the hourly rate include telephony and recordings?

Every rate above is from a published page as read on 2 November 2026: Clutch's provider cards for the hourly bands, and our own pricing pages for the appointment and system figures. This is general information, not legal advice.
faqs: How much do B2B telemarketing services cost per hour?

On Clutch's telemarketing rankings page read on 2 November 2026, 36 of the 42 providers on the first page listed a self-reported rate under $25 an hour, 4 listed $25 to $49, 1 listed $50 to $99 and 1 listed $150 to $199. Of the 48 minimum-project badges we counted, 31 read $1,000 and up, 10 read $5,000, 3 read $10,000, 2 read $50,000 and 2 read $100,000.
How much does a qualified B2B appointment cost?

Our published lead generation packages are $2,997 a month for 20 to 40 qualified appointments, $5,997 for 40 to 80 and $9,997 and up for 80 to 150 or more, which implies roughly $67 to $150 per appointment depending on the package and the number delivered.
Is outsourced telemarketing cheaper than an AI calling system?

They buy different things. An agent in the under-$25 band is under $4,000 a month for 160 hours (for example $3,840 at an assumed $24 an hour) before data, telephony and compliance; an AI calling deployment on our pages is from $2,497 to build and from $1,997 a month to run, with telephony and voice billed by those vendors. AI suits inbound qualification and consented follow-up at volume; cold outbound by an AI voice faces consent and state rules that live agents do not.
Who is liable if a telemarketing vendor breaks the TCPA?

The seller can be. The TCPA allows $500 per violation, up to three times that for willful or knowing violations, and under the FCC's 2013 DISH ruling a seller may be held vicariously liable for a vendor's calls under federal common law agency principles. Several states, including Georgia and New York, write vendor liability into their own telemarketing statutes.
Do B2B telemarketers have to register with states?

Often, unless an exemption applies. Six of the seven states in our hub require registration or a licence, from $50 in California to $1,500 in Florida, with bonds of $10,000 to $100,000, and California's applies only to sellers whose pitch meets section 17511.1. B2B exemptions vary: New York exempts most business-to-business calls, Florida exempts B2B sales by sellers with three years under one name and 50 percent repeat business sales or where the buyer resells or manufactures, Pennsylvania covers only consumer goods or services, and Texas and Washington exempt sales to businesses that resell or manufacture with the goods.
What should a telemarketing contract specify?

The definition of a qualified appointment and what happens on no-shows, who scrubs the list and how often, which states are registered and under which exemptions, the calling hours enforced by local time, the abandonment rate and dropped-call handling, how opt-outs are captured and shared, and whether the hourly rate includes telephony and recordings.
